_comment: Hand-written prose per code (from docs/memory-model.md section 7). The example program, its .diag line and the compiler output are generated from compiler/testdata/memory by gen-diagnostics.mjs.

M0101.title: Use after free
M0101.meaning: A value is read, called or borrowed after `free()`, `close()` or the end of a `use {}` block released it. It also fires for a borrowed alias (`val b = a`) or a `@Borrowed` result once the owner it derives from was freed. If only one control-flow path frees the value, the message says it "may have been freed".
M0101.fix: Move the use before the release, or release later. If you need the value after the call that frees it, keep ownership (do not pass it to an `@Owned` parameter) or copy out the data you need first.

M0102.title: Leak: allocation is never released
M0102.meaning: An owning variable, parameter or field leaves its scope while it still holds a live allocation from a `Deallocating` allocator (`Heap`, `Pool`) or an unclosed `Arena`/`Pool` resource. The label names the path that leaks: end of scope, early return, `break`, `continue`, `throw`, not released on all branches, overwritten, result discarded, or an `@Owned` parameter that is never freed.
M0102.fix: Release the value on every path (`x.free()`, `x.close()`, or wrap it in `x.use { }` for `AutoCloseable` classes), or hand ownership on (return it as `@Owned`, pass it to an `@Owned` parameter, store it in an owning field). Put the release in a `finally` block when exceptions are involved.

M0103.title: Double free
M0103.meaning: `free()`, `close()` or the end of a `use {}` block is applied to a value that is already freed on some path that reaches it, including a free in a loop body that runs twice.
M0103.fix: Delete the second release. If the value is conditionally freed earlier, restructure so that exactly one path frees it, or free it only in one place (for example a `finally`).

M0104.title: Use after move
M0104.meaning: A value is used after ownership moved away from it: through `x.move()`, by passing it to an `@Owned` parameter, by storing it in an owning field, by capturing it in a thread lambda, or by a `use {}`/`close()` that consumed it. A move inside a loop that is hit again on the next iteration is reported too.
M0104.fix: Use the new owner instead of the old variable, or write `val b = a` (a borrowed alias) if no transfer was intended. Inside loops, re-initialise the variable before the back edge.

M0105.title: Escape from a Scoped allocator
M0105.meaning: A value allocated in an `Arena` leaves the scope of that arena: it is returned, becomes the result of the `use {}` block, is stored in a field of a longer-lived object or a global, or is captured by a lambda that outlives the arena.
M0105.fix: Return a value that needs no allocation (`Int`, `Boolean`, ...), copy the data out, or let the caller own the arena: declare the function with `context(a: Arena)` so that the objects live in the caller's region.

M0106.title: Individual free of a Scoped object
M0106.meaning: `free()` is called on an object of an arena, or an arena object is passed to an `@Owned` parameter (the callee could free it). Arena objects have no individual release: the whole arena dies together.
M0106.fix: Remove the `free()`. The arena reclaims the object when it is closed. If an arena object has resources, call its `close()` directly (that does not release memory).

M0107.title: Release of a non-owned value
M0107.meaning: `free()`, `close()` or `use {}` is applied to a value this code does not own: a parameter that is not `@Owned`, a `@Borrowed` slot, an alias, a Managed object, or a variable whose ownership was already moved away. The same code reports `alias.use { }` and passing an alias to an `@Owned` parameter.
M0107.fix: If the function should take over the object, declare the parameter `@Owned` (and let callers move into it). Otherwise leave the release to the owner.

M0108.title: Wrong allocator when freeing
M0108.meaning: `alloc.free(x)` names an allocator, but `x` demonstrably came from a different one, as far as the compiler can tell statically.
M0108.fix: Use `x.free()`, which finds the right allocator by itself, or name the allocator that actually produced the object.

M0109.title: Loan is stored or returned as owned
M0109.meaning: A borrowed value (a parameter without `@Owned`, an alias, a `@Borrowed` result) flows into an owning field, an owning return, an `@Owned` argument, or is captured by an escaping lambda. The loan would outlive the owner it was lent from.
M0109.fix: Make the parameter `@Owned` (and move at the call site), or declare the function's return type `@Borrowed` so that it returns a loan instead of ownership.

M0110.title: Violation of the Strict/Managed boundary
M0110.meaning: A tracked (Strict) value crosses into Managed code in a way the checker cannot follow: it goes into a Kotlin collection, into a field of a Managed class, into a Managed function parameter that is not `@Borrowed`, or Managed code calls a Strict function that takes or returns ownership.
M0110.fix: Build your own container class from owning fields, wrap the Managed call in a Strict function that frees internally, or mark the Managed parameter `@Borrowed` if it really only borrows.

M0111.title: Invalid ownership annotation
M0111.meaning: `@Owned` is placed on a type that has no ownership (primitives, `String`, Managed classes), `@Owned` and `@Borrowed` are combined, or `@Borrowed` contradicts an owning return.

M0112.title: Owning value in an escaping lambda
M0112.meaning: A lambda that is not inlined and is not a thread boundary captures an owning value. Closures as owners (move capture) are not supported yet.
M0112.fix: Pass the value to the code that needs it as an explicit parameter, or read the data you need (`b.v`) before creating the lambda and capture that instead.

M0113.title: Owned field stays moved
M0113.meaning: A value was moved out of an owning field with `s.item.move()` and the field was not given a valid value again before the next call or the end of the function.
M0113.fix: Assign the field again (a new value or `null`) before the function returns or calls anything else.

M0114.title: Ambiguous allocator
M0114.meaning: Two or more allocator context parameters are visible at the same level (`context(a: Arena, h: Heap)`), so the compiler cannot tell which one an allocation should use.
M0114.fix: Nest the contexts: `context(h) { ... }` inside the outer one. The innermost context wins.

M0115.title: Arena object owns a foreign reference
M0115.meaning: An arena never runs `dispose` on its objects, so an object in an arena must not own anything that needs releasing. A reference-counted `String`, a Managed object, or a Heap/Pool object flows into an owning field of an arena object. String literals are static and allowed.
M0115.fix: Mark the field `@Borrowed` (non-owning; you are then responsible for the lifetime), keep only primitives, literals and objects of the same arena in arena objects, or avoid the arena for this data.

M0201.title: Allocation moved to the stack
M0201.meaning: An informational note that an allocation does not escape and lives on the stack. It is specified in docs/memory-model.md (shown only with `-Minfo`), but no `M0201` exists in the compiler yet.
M0201.fix: Nothing to fix: it is not an error and never changes whether a program is accepted.

M0202.title: Allocation in an arena loop
M0202.meaning: An allocation inside a loop uses a `Scoped` arena. Nothing is freed until the arena closes, so memory grows with every iteration. This is a warning: the program is still accepted (`-Werror` turns it into a failure).
M0202.fix: Hoist the allocation out of the loop, or reset/recreate the arena per iteration.

M0203.title: Large object on the stack
M0203.meaning: A warning for objects larger than a size threshold (default 64 KB in the spec) that would be placed on the stack. Specified in docs/memory-model.md, not implemented in the compiler yet (it belongs to the escape-analysis work).

M0204.title: No allocator for an escaping Strict value
M0204.meaning: In a Strict file there is no default allocator. A value that escapes (is returned, stored, passed as `@Owned`) needs one from a visible `context(...)` parameter or from an `@AllocatedBy` class annotation. Non-escaping values simply live on the stack and need none.
M0204.fix: Add `context(h: Heap)` to the function, wrap the call in `context(Heap()) { ... }`, or annotate the class with `@AllocatedBy(Heap::class)`.

M0205.title: Allocation in a @NoAlloc function
M0205.meaning: A function marked `@NoAlloc` contains an allocation that is not on the stack (it escapes) or calls `alloc.allocate(...)`. Only the function's own body is checked; calls to other functions are not followed yet.
M0205.fix: Take the object as a parameter, keep it non-escaping so that it lives on the stack, or remove `@NoAlloc`.

M0206.title: Object leaves the thread but its allocator is not ThreadSafe
M0206.meaning: A value from an allocator that does not implement `ThreadSafe` (`Arena`, `Pool`), or the allocator itself, is captured by a thread lambda (`spawn { }`).
M0206.fix: Allocate the shared objects from a `Heap`, which is `ThreadSafe`.
